For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "9/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Application order (standard)
On each invoice, the billing system applies adjustments in this order:
1. **Included usage** in the customer’s package/free tier (if applicable)
2. **Contracted unit prices** (including any negotiated discount)
3. **Credits** (promotional/contracted/service), applied to the eligible usage subtotal
4. Taxes and non-creditable line items
Important: credits offset charges; they do **not change recorded usage quantities**.
### Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
If the meter spec distinguishes cached vs uncached billed tokens, credits apply to the final **billed** quantities after cache and dedupe logic. Any customer-visible statement about caching must use approved language from Legal (see related page)."}, {"source": "sources/linear/design/PM-9031-tiered-burst-quotas-overage-grace-periods.json", "chunk": "5/6", "kind": "Linear issue", "title": "Tiered burst quotas, soft/hard rate limits and overage billing policy", "status": "In Review", "date": "2025-03-05", "text": "  - E2E tests covering token-level metering, burst buffer exhaustion, and mid-cycle upgrades exist and pass in CI
  - Billing exports include overage line items with plan id and unit pricing and reconcile to invoices in staging environment
billing_acceptance_criteria:
  - When a hosted account exhausts monthly baseline and has overage enabled, an overage invoice line is created automatically at the next billing run and shows items: units, unit price, and total
  - If overage is disabled, customer receives console notification and API calls are blocked with a clear error code: quota_exhausted_no_overage
  - Grace period: accounts that newly enable overage mid-cycle receive a configurable 48h grace window where overage is tracked but not billed; billing shows a 'grace' flag in staging exports
  - Proration: when a customer upgrades mid-cycle to a higher plan, remaining quota is prorated and overage thresholds are recomputed; tests must show correct ledger adjustments"}]}

body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.
## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.
## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.

body: ## Purpose
How solutions engineers estimate a prospect's monthly tokens before a quote. Estimates use an approximate tokenizer and round up 10% for safety. This page is about forecasting before purchase. It does not explain how billed tokens are counted on an invoice; for that, see the token accounting pages and the billing routing page.
## Method
1. Sample 100 representative requests.
2. Count characters and divide by 4 for English text.
3. Multiply by expected monthly volume and add 10%.
_Last reviewed 2026-02-09._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "3/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Definitions (use these terms consistently)
- **Meter / billable unit:** The unit recorded by billing telemetry and used to produce invoices. Example: **billed_tokens** for Hosted API.
- **Raw tokens vs billed tokens:** Raw tokens may include uncached or pre-dedupe counts. **Billed tokens** are the invoicing unit after billing rules (dedupe/idempotency, cache-hit attribution rules, etc.). Credits and discounts apply to **billed** usage only.
- **Discount:** A reduction in price per unit (e.g., $/1M tokens) or a percentage reduction on usage charges.
- **Credit:** A dollar value that offsets charges on invoices (a “coupon” balance). Credits have **no cash value** and are not refundable unless required by contract or law.
- **Service credit:** A credit issued for SLA/non-conformance or billing errors.
- **Promotional credit:** A credit granted for trial, marketing campaigns, partnerships, or sales incentives.
- **Contracted credit:** A credit explicitly included in an Order Form/MSA as part of commercial terms."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-20", "text": "title: Batch API Pricing (2027)

body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.
## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.
## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.
_Last reviewed 2027-01-20._"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/customer-facing-marketplace-faq-draft.json", "chunk": "9/19", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Redwood Inference Marketplace FAQ (Customer-facing) — Draft", "status": "draft", "date": "2026-02-14", "text": "## 4) Billing, metering, and invoices
### Q: How will I be billed if I purchase via marketplace?
Marketplace purchases are billed through your cloud provider (AWS or GCP). Redwood reports metered usage (as applicable) to the marketplace, and the charges appear on your cloud bill under the Redwood marketplace product.
### Q: What usage is metered?
Metering depends on your SKU/offer. Common examples:
- Hosted API: usage-based (e.g., tokens processed, embeddings units), billed per the marketplace dimensions for the purchased SKU
- Dedicated capacity: reserved capacity dimension(s) or committed spend, depending on your offer structure
- Add-ons: may be billed as a recurring dimension (e.g., per month) or tied to usage, depending on the marketplace configuration
Your marketplace offer details define the billing dimensions and unit pricing."}]}

Not always. An internal retry that’s deduplicated using an idempotency key is non-billable. But a retry that runs as a separate, non-deduplicated request can add billed usage for the tokens processed; a timeout or disconnect doesn’t necessarily mean zero usage if tokens were processed or streamed before it stopped.
